data_fields.name: engageDelayTicks
data_fields.donor_constant: count = 1500 animation frames before the chase branch runs

data_fields.name: landRadius
data_fields.donor_constant: 30 px Manhattan distance to home lands the sprite

data_fields.name: speed
data_fields.donor_constant: 3 or 5 px per animation frame along 8 directions (table)

data_fields.name: maxTurnPerTick
data_fields.donor_constant: one 45-degree step per heading refresh; refresh every 4th sprite cycle (mask 3)

data_fields.name: wanderPoint
data_fields.donor_constant: random point on the map at spawn, plus 8 px offset

data_fields.name: monsterArrivalRadius
data_fields.donor_constant: 60 px Manhattan; first arrival sends it home, second ends it

data_fields.name: monsterTurnChance
data_fields.donor_constant: Random.getChance(10): bit mask test, about 1 in 4 (computed)

best_idea: Give a chaser an engage delay counted in server ticks, a priority list with a fallback to home, and a landing radius around home, so it leashes back to its anchor when there is no valid target.
decision_why: The delay, the priority-then-home destination and the landing radius are the right leash shape for a single fast chaser or boss; take it with server ticks and plain probability fields, pick targets from the engine's hate table, and do not take the frame counter, the 8-way quantised movement, or the first-in-list choice.
acceptance: Server test: chaser with engageDelayTicks 10 and home at (0, 0), starting at (200, 0) with wander point (200, 200): for 10 ticks it steers toward the wander point and not toward a player at (50, 0); after the delay with a live primary it steers toward the primary; with no primary and a live secondary it steers toward the secondary; once within landRadius 30 (Manhattan) of home it lands and does not move again.
